subject: Clarion Health — Dedicated GPU mix recommendation and cost/latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alex Goldman <alex@clarionhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@clarionhealth.com
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing — initial requirements

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our platform team sent over estimated QPS and typical prompt sizes — mostly clinical summarization and a mix of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with ~2.5k token contexts on average and peak 8k. We need Redwood Dedicated recommendations for GPU SKUs and a proposed fleet mix for the first 12 months (proof-of-value to full prod). Key constraints:
- Predictable 99th pctl latency under 400ms for short prompts (<=1k tokens).
- Support long-context summarization up to 32k in degraded but acceptable latency.
- Tight cost controls for year 1.

Can you outline tradeoffs between H100 / A100 (40/80GB variants) and L4 for our mix and give a recommended allocation and fallback strategy? Also include what we should expect in terms of memory headroom, batching, and KV cache considerations.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Goldman
Director, Platform Engineering
Clarion Health


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Goldman <alex@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing — initial requirements

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements. I've pulled our initial sizing and cost model (attached) and sketched an ops-safe fleet recommendation below. High level takeaways first, then a recommended fleet mix and ops notes.

Quick summary:
- H100 (80GB): best for sustained high-throughput 32k-context runs and aggressive FP8/quantized inference of large encoder-decoder models. Highest per-unit throughput for long-context, but highest $/hour.
- A100 (40/80GB): cost-effective for most 8k/16k use cases and offers better price/perf for FP16 workloads. A100 80GB parity with H100 on memory but lower raw inference throughput for some large attention patterns.
- L4 (24GB): excellent low-cost option for embeddings, short-generation, and serving distilled or quantized model variants for conversational traffic. Lower memory and slower for very long contexts.

Recommended 12-month starter mix (proof-of-value -> ramp):
- Stage 0 (PoV, months 0-3): 60% A100-80 / 30% L4 / 10% H100-80 (small H100 pool for long-context nightly jobs)
- Stage 1 (scale, months 4-12): 45% A100-80 / 30% H100-80 / 25% L4 (shift to more H100 as long-context usage grows)

Rationale: A100-80 gives predictable memory headroom for 8k-16k average contexts with efficient batching; L4 keeps unit costs low for high-QPS short prompts and embeddings; H100 is reserved for heavy-duty 32k runs and throughput spikes where latency matters.

Ops & caching notes:
- KV cache sizing: long-context summarization benefits from prefix caching; allocate 1.5–2x model KV memory for headroom when planning H100 pools.
- Batching: use continuous batching on A100 pools for cost efficiency; keep H100 pools tuned for smaller batch sizes when SLOs require low p99 latency.
- Quantization: enable 4/8-bit quantization for non-critical generations to boost throughput on A100 and L4; certify output quality on your eval prompt set before enabling.

I'll loop in Ben for the raw throughput models and Dev for the fallback/rollout policy. Attached: clarion-sku-analysis-v1.xlsx and a cost model CSV.

Next steps: 1) confirm if Clarion prefers more conservative latency (p99 300ms) vs cost ceiling; 2) we can run a 2-week PoV with a 10-node hybrid pool and provide telemetry.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Alex Goldman <alex@clarionhealth.com>

Date: 2027-12-01T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing — initial requirements

Alex/Sofia — added a deeper perf sketch and a conservative capacity plan. Key numbers (ballpark, compressed):
- A100-80: ~1.0x baseline throughput for 8k-context bi-encoder/decoder workloads at FP16 with batching 8–16; comfortably handles most steady-state production traffic.
- H100-80: ~1.7x throughput vs A100 for 16k+ attention heavy workloads at our tuned kernels, and better multi-query throughput for high-concurrency.
- L4 (24GB): ~0.35x throughput vs A100 on large models but ~0.5–0.8x on distilled or smaller models; great for embedding & chat where latency SLOs are modest.

Suggested operational fallback:
- Primary routing: shortest-latency policy to A100 if within capacity.
- Fallback 1: L4 for short prompt routes (<=1k tokens) and for embedding-heavy spikes.
- Fallback 2: H100 for queued long-context jobs or when A100 p99 latency breaches threshold (migrate active requests or fallback to partial-response + async completion).

Cost sensitivity: if Clarion's target is to cap host spend in year-1, recommend moving more workloads to L4 + aggressive quantization, and using H100 only for scheduled long-context processing windows.

I attach the conservative node counts in clarion-cost-model.csv (sheet: conservative). Happy to walk through the math.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications: 1) our clinical summarization model is a 30B encoder-decoder variant (we plan to use a 16k context by default), 2) peak concurrent real-time requests hit ~120 QPS during business hours.

What minimum H100 count would you recommend to keep 99th pctl <400ms for the 16k default summarization when A100 is saturated? We prefer not to over-provision but want a sensible failover. Also can you flag any model changes (quantization or distillation) we should try first to reduce cost?

Best,
Alex

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Goldman <alex@clarionhealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing — initial requirements

Alex — quick reply with concrete numbers based on the 30B / 16k workload and your 120 QPS peak:
- Minimum H100 nodes for failover (kept warm): 4 x H100-80 GPUs (N=4) — this covers ~25–30 concurrent 16k summarization sessions at p99 <400ms using tuned kernels and FP8 where quality is acceptable.
- A100 pool sizing for steady-state: 12 x A100-80 GPUs to absorb ~70–80 QPS of mixed-length requests with batching enabled. Remaining short requests should be routed to L4.
- L4 sizing for short prompts & embeddings: 6 x L4 nodes (estimate) to cover 30–40 QPS of short jobs with very low cost.

Notes on model changes:
- Try 8-bit or 4-bit quantization on a shadow branch for your eval set; many 30B models maintain acceptable ROUGE/ROUGE-L/clinical fidelity with 8-bit.
- Distill a 7–13B assistant model for the chat/short-answers surface; keep 30B for summarization and heavy RAG when fidelity matters.

Operational recommendation: keep H100 warm rather than cold-started, and use auto-failover routing that prefers A100 until p99 thresholds are approached. We'll include a canary rollout plan in the PoV.

— Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
